// This fixture does every one of the things the neighbouring fixture does, done
// the way the rules allow, and it must produce no finding at all.
//
// It is the near miss rather than an obviously clean file. Each line below is
// one character or one import away from a line in breaks-every-rule.go.txt: an
// integer comparison rather than a floating point one, a package that parses an
// address rather than one that opens a connection, a fixture path that stays
// inside the package. A reader that fired on any of these would be a reader
// nobody could keep switched on.
package example

import (
	"net/url"
	"os"
	"testing"

	"github.com/iderex/schallweg/acoustic/approx"
)

func TestTheSameThingsDoneLegally(t *testing.T) {
	got := compute()

	// The comparison the rule wants instead, with the tolerance stated.
	approx.Equal(t, "R_w", got, 61.3, 0.05)

	// An integer comparison. One character from a floating point literal and
	// entirely legitimate.
	if bands := count(); bands != 16 {
		t.Errorf("got %d bands, want 16", bands)
	}

	// A committed fixture, read from this package's own testdata directory.
	data, err := os.ReadFile("testdata/spectrum.csv")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	_ = data

	// Parsing an address is not reaching one.
	u, err := url.Parse("https://example.invalid/")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	_ = u
}
